head: 9a4c4ab
target: Ship own-your-diff as one marketplace plugin that installs into Claude Code, Droid, and Codex: harness hooks that re-install the git gate in every opted-in clone, a PreToolUse guard that keeps gate bypass in human hands, and an installer that reaches every harness on PATH and makes Codex trust the hooks.
incidental: selftest restructure: repo-root paths and isolated HOME/git-config test scaffolding

questions.prompt: Before this branch, own-your-diff was plain scripts in a repo. Why does it now ship as one marketplace plugin whose .claude-plugin/ manifest and hooks/hooks.json all three harnesses read, instead of keeping loose scripts or maintaining one package per harness?

options.label: A per-harness package would drift; one tree that every harness reads means the gate, the guard, and the skill ship and update together everywhere
Only a marketplace plugin may run a hook at session start in any harness
Installing as a plugin makes the git pre-push hook unnecessary
Only a marketplace package may write files under the user's home directory

key_points: all three harnesses read the same .claude-plugin/ and hooks/hooks.json layout, so one source tree installs into all three
one source of truth: the gate, the guard, and the skill update together; per-harness forks would drift apart

questions.prompt: A teammate makes a fresh clone of an opted-in repo and starts a session in Droid. What does the SessionStart hook do in that clone, and why is that hook needed at all?

options.label: It runs quizgate sync, which puts the gate on the shared bin dir and writes the missing pre-push hook; the committed .own-your-diff marker travels with clones but the git hook never does
It writes .own-your-diff into the clone, since the marker is per-machine
It holds the session start until the author passes a quiz
Nothing: sync only runs inside the plugin's own repository

key_points: the opt-in marker is committed and travels with clones, while .git/hooks/pre-push does not
SessionStart runs quizgate sync in every session, so the gate self-heals in every clone of an opted-in repo
it is best-effort and must never fail the session; enforcement stays with the git hook

questions.prompt: The SessionStart hook could exec the gate straight out of the plugin directory through ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}. Instead it runs quizgate sync, which copies the gate to a stable bin dir (default ~/.local/bin). Why is the stable copy the right shape?

options.label: The pre-push hook runs inside git, outside any harness, where CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset and the plugin's install path moves on update; the git hook needs a stable path it can find on its own
The plugin directory is read-only once the plugin is installed
Running the in-plugin copy would retrigger the PreToolUse guard on every session
Git refuses to exec any hook script that lives inside a plugin directory

key_points: git hooks run outside the harness, where no plugin path or CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is available
plugin install paths are versioned and move on update, while the bin dir is stable
the pre-push hook locates the gate on PATH with a fixed fallback, and sync keeps that copy current

questions.prompt: A fourth harness, amp, appears next month and reads the same plugin layout. Where does support for it go, and what changes?

options.label: An amp_install function in install.sh plus amp in the PATH-detection loop; the plugin tree and hooks stay as they are
A fork of .claude-plugin/ and hooks/ into an amp-specific layout
Nothing: install.sh already installs into any harness binary it finds on PATH
A second plugins entry in marketplace.json, one per harness

key_points: the shared manifest and hooks need no change; only install.sh learns the new harness
add a per-harness install function and a name in the PATH-detection loop
if the new harness gates hooks behind a trust model like Codex, its install step must also write the trust entries

questions.prompt: Which of these agent commands does the PreToolUse guard deny? Pick every option that holds; the exact set passes.

options.label: git push --no-verify origin main
git config core.hooksPath /dev/null
git config --get core.hooksPath
git commit --no-verify -m fix

key_points: the guard denies push --no-verify: bypassing the quiz gate is the human's call, never the agent's
it denies core.hooksPath changes, which would silently disable the pre-push hook, but allows reads of the setting
commit --no-verify is allowed: it bypasses no part of this gate

questions.prompt: Suppose install.sh installs the plugin into Codex but the trust step never runs. What does the gate look like on that machine, and why does the design write Codex's hook-trust entries at install time instead of leaving them to the TUI's approval prompt?
key_points: Codex skips plugin hooks until their definition hash is trusted, so session-start and the guard never run there
fresh clones of opted-in repos never get the pre-push hook, the agent never hears the opt-in reminder, and nothing warns the user: the gate is silently off
the installer writes the same hooks.state entries the Codex TUI writes when the user approves, so running install.sh is the consent moment; trust is automated exactly once, at install time

questions.prompt: In an opted-in repo with the pre-push hook installed and quizgate on PATH, an agent runs git push --no-verify with unquizzed commits pending. Which of these hold? Pick every option that holds; the exact set passes.

options.label: The PreToolUse guard denies the command before git ever runs it
If the guard misses the command, the unquizzed commits reach the remote, because --no-verify tells git to skip the pre-push hook
If the guard misses the command, the pre-push hook still blocks the push, so the commits stay local
A human running the same push --no-verify in their own terminal is breaking the design

key_points: the guard is the first line: it denies the agent's --no-verify push before git runs
--no-verify makes git skip the pre-push hook, so if the guard misses the command the unquizzed push succeeds; the git hook cannot backstop a bypass
a human pushing --no-verify from their own terminal is allowed by design: the guard only sees the agent's tool calls, and bypass is the human's call
